summary: Kickoff for a 3-week POC focused on throughput/latency benchmarks and executive readout. Agreed access steps, success criteria, and a mid-point review; owners assigned for benchmark artifacts and infra access.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-05 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jill (BrightCart Head of ML), Samir (Platform), Karen (Product), Tom (Security), Devon (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- POC length proposed 3 weeks: kickoff, access & baseline, mid-point sync, exec readout.
- Success criteria: p95 latency <= 600ms for 256 token generation on pilot workload, throughput 1200 tokens/sec aggregate, embedding recall target > 0.82 on eval set, cost target ~ $0.02/1k tokens (post-quantization).

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I think we have most people. Hi Jill, Samir, Karen, Tom, good to see you. We're here to lock down the POC timeline and milestones and make sure we have the right access and benchmarks in place.
[00:18] Jill Park: Yep, hi Alex. Quick note — our execs want a crisp readout in 3 weeks that shows clear perf and cost delta vs our current hosted endpoints.
[00:27] Samir Patel: Also need to confirm security gating. We'll need to know exact network changes for VPC peering, and Tom will sign off.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Great. I'll talk through the proposed milestone plan and the benchmark matrix, then we can assign owners. Marco will chime in on the test harness.
[00:45] Marco Ruiz: Yup — we've got a lightweight load generator and a Jupyter runbook. We'll provide a script that hits both Redwood hosted and the dedicated variant so you can see the delta. There may be minor naming weirdness in the logs — apologies if you see "Redwood Dedicate" in places, it's a transcription of an internal tag.
[01:02] Karen Liu: Quick question up front — what's the minimal dataset you need for meaningful evals? We can't share PII.
[01:10] Priya Nair: We ask for a 10k sample of sanitized customer interactions (text only), plus a 500-example eval holdout for quality checks. If you can't share real data, synthetic or redacted will work for perf and routing tests but quality assessments will be limited.
[01:28] Jill Park: 10k seems doable if Samir can create an anonymized S3 path. We'll aim for a 1-week turnaround.
[01:35] Tom Reyes: On telemetry — we need to limit logs to non-PII and only aggregate metrics. What's your default retention?
[01:42] Alex Chen: For the POC we use short retention by default (30 days) but we can configure it. We'll send the security deck and telemetry options.
[01:50] Tom Reyes: Please include specifics about KMS integration and whether we can supply our HSM keys.
[01:55] Priya Nair: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer KMS, and for the POC we can emulate the keyflow. We'll include the KMS notes in the security pack.

Topics covered:
- POC duration & milestones
- Access & infra requirements (VPC, IAM, sample data)
- Benchmarking matrix: latency/throughput/cost/quality
- Roles and stakeholders + sign-off criteria for exec readout
- Potential blockers (compliance, data timing, perf variance)

[02:20] Marco Ruiz: Walkthrough of milestone timeline:
  - Week 0 (this week): kickoff, sign NDAs if needed, collect contact points, share benchmark spreadsheet and runbook.
  - Week 1: Access setup (VPC peering or Private env), sample data ingest, baseline run on existing endpoints.
  - Week 2: Redwood runs controlled benchmarks (varying sequence lengths: 64/256/1024), tuning phase (batching, quantization).
  - Week 3: Mid-point check (30 min), final tuning and exec readout prep, present results to execs end of week.

[03:05] Jill Park: That sequence is fine. Can you be explicit about gating? What determines go/no-go to the exec readout?
[03:13] Priya Nair: Good point. Proposed gating:
  - Access: we must be able to run at least 3 baseline experiments within 48h of access provision.
  - Perf: p95 latency threshold — we proposed <= 600ms for the 256-token typical path; throughput target 1100–1300 tokens/sec aggregate for the dedicated pool.
  - Quality: embeddings recall >= 0.82 on your holdout; generation quality no regression vs your current baselines (we'll quantify with eval prompts).
  - Cost: baseline cost per 1k tokens after recommended quantization should be within 30% of your target (Karen: you gave a target earlier?).

[03:58] Karen Liu: We were targeting roughly $0.02/1k tokens for inference on the high-volume path. If Redwood's numbers are within 30% that's acceptable for execs to consider next step.
[04:08] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll include a cost breakdown and expected delta for the configurations we test (4-bit quant, batch size choices, caching).

[04:25] Samir Patel: On infra specifics: we prefer VPC peering to minimize egress complexity. We'll need a detailed network diagram and a contact for the peering window. Also need clear ports and subnets.
[04:38] Priya Nair: We'll send a minimal peering checklist. For the POC we can also run in a private customer-controlled deployment if you prefer, but peering is faster to get started.
[04:50] Tom Reyes: If it's peering, we need a security review. Will Redwood provide an architecture diagram and ACL list?
[04:56] Marco Ruiz: Yes — architecture diagram, ports, and logs collected will be in the runbook. Expect a short doc in the shared folder.

[05:12] Devon (SRE): How do you handle load shaping and KV cache warmup? In prod we see cold-start variability.
[05:21] Marco Ruiz: Good question. The runbook includes a warmup phase (1000 prefix tokens per worker) and we'll run repeated passes to stabilize KV cache. We'll also provide a reproducible load pattern and seeds so you can compare. Note: sometimes transcriptions show KV cache as K V cache, apologies.

[05:40] Jill Park: For quality metrics, will you run automated evals or manual review?
[05:45] Priya Nair: Both. Automated metrics (ROUGE, embedding recall, semantic search hit rate) for the bulk, and a small manual spot-check set for subjective quality. We'll align on the eval prompt set.

[06:02] Karen Liu: For the exec readout, we want a 20-minute slide deck that includes a one-slide TL;DR (numbers), one slide on tests, one on security/compliance, one on recommended next steps with cost delta.
[06:13] Alex Chen: We'll own the deck and draft it after mid-point. BrightCart should provide an executive summary slide that states acceptance criteria and business ask.

[06:25] Tom Reyes: A couple red flags: telemetry containing raw text is not allowed, and we need an audit trail for who accesses keys and logs.
[06:33] Alex Chen: Understood — we will anonymize transcripts and provide role-based access for logs. We'll include an audit log export sample in the security package.

[06:44] Marco Ruiz: Back to performance: desired sequence length distribution?
[06:48] Jill Park: 70% at 256 tokens, 20% at 64 tokens, 10% at long tail 1k tokens. Most of our traffic is short-medium.
[06:58] Priya Nair: We'll prioritize the 256 path for SLO tuning, and also run a long-tail run to show degradation behavior. For cost estimates we'll show per-token cost at each quantization level and with/without prefix cache.

[07:12] Samir Patel: Are there any limitations on the number of concurrent streams? Our plan is to ramp to 50 concurrent user sessions during the POC to simulate peak.
[07:20] Marco Ruiz: That's fine. We'll run step-ramp tests up to 100 concurrent to show headroom. The dedicated pool sizing recommendation will be part of the deliverable.

[07:33] Karen Liu: Timeline recap?
[07:36] Priya Nair: Kickoff today (8/5). By 8/8 Redwood shares benchmark sheet and runbook. BrightCart provisions S3 sample + IAM by 8/12. Redwood completes initial runs and tuning by 8/19; schedule mid-point 8/21; exec readout week of 8/25 (end of that week).
[07:54] Jill Park: That schedule maps to our internal readiness. We need at least 72 hours between mid-point and exec deck draft for internal review.
[07:59] Alex Chen: We'll plan for that.

[08:05] Tom Reyes: Small ask — include a short checklist for legal/procurement if we go to reserved capacity next.
[08:11] Alex Chen: We'll add a one-page procurement checklist (terms, compliance prerequisites, expected lead times).

[08:20] Karen Liu: Any competitors or comparatives you plan to include? Execs want a quick competitor show — e.g., Anthropic and Vertex notes.
[08:27] Alex Chen: We'll include a high-level slide comparing latency/cost points vs Anthropic and Vertex where public data exists, plus our run-time measured values.

[08:35] Priya Nair: I'll note out-of-scope items: on-prem full air-gapped install is out of scope for this 3-week POC; that's a separate engagement. Also long-term retention/archival compliance beyond 90 days is not in the POC.

[08:47] Jill Park: Good to know.

Final recap and owners:
- Alex: benchmark sheet + exec deck draft (post mid-point)
- Priya/Marco: runbook, perf tests, and tuning recommendations
- Samir: infra provisioning (IAM, S3, VPC peering)
- Tom: security acceptance and telemetry constraints

[09:20] Alex Chen: Any final Qs?
[09:23] Samir Patel: One more — do you have a baseline cost calc for both hosted and dedicated for expected traffic?
[09:28] Alex Chen: We'll include a simple cost model in the spreadsheet with assumptions (requests/sec, average tokens per request, quant level).

[09:35] Karen Liu: OK, thanks everyone. Look forward to the benchmark sheet.
[09:39] Jill Park: Thanks — we'll aim to have Samir provision the sample data by the 12th.
[09:42] Alex Chen: Great. We'll follow up with the runbook and security docs and schedule the mid-point. Thanks all.
